problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy),\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

examples.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/f18ed650b92e1d02e809d5eb997a231ec9a118da285292f88339bb4fdc3aaf95.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/613ba027e9564812a8e050efd69fd98fff3f614f7d2ec69eeb787c628ccabd12.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/87579b882ca6d8c92d4a7adfed575873fd07c36ab20251722c2cc8fc0f0328e8.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})=3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/dcff4801886965e64a2e145869bd8c1ee4559c8cbe458661d53ad06ecd6ddb30.png)

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/e73720f8e1c08238a11ab557a3e515a214b3b9ed76000ca900ccf801de5d76c4.png) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/6d7d1453ae6acad9a4d99359bcf40f4e90ac3383ade8a0aff58c82097fe37fde.png)

The tangent to $f$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
z - f(\mathbf a) = \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $f(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068404/assets/5c360a03ebca35811d9d95508cf4dc08481865040c64aa6f608202de88af98f2.png)

$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by

{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y &  \\ y &  \\  & 1\end{aligned}].

feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+{y}^{2})=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy+{y}^{2})=x+2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x+2y \\ y & x \\ \frac{1}{x} & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the missing entries are $x+2y,\,$ $x,\,$ and $\frac{1}{x}.$
